newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil remains slow, barge premiums slip.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil remains slow, barge premiums slip.

text.p: NWE gas oil trade continued in the doldrums on Thursday, slowed by uncertainty over whether any of Tuesday's record high 865,100 tonne delivery into the November IPE futures expiry would reappear on the market.

"It's a game of nerves and only time will show who the winner is," one trader said, referring to efforts by the dominant long and dominant short in the contract to convince the market that they were comfortable with their positions.
Dec IPE finished $3 firmer at $219.25 per tonne but well below the day's high of $223 amid weakness on the expiring Dec Brent crude contract and unimpressive NYMEX futures.

Barge premiums slipped amid signs of oversupply in the Rotterdam area but those for cargoes held steady with traders saying most remaining parcels of recently-arrived U.S.-origin arbitrage material appeared to have found homes.
A barge of heating oil fob ARA traded down $1 at Dec IPE +$5. A 3,000 tonne barge of low sulphur diesel traded at Dec IPE +$12.50 Nov 16-20, down from Dec +$14/16.
"There is a lot of (low sulphur diesel) material stored. People seem to be desperate to sell," one said.
Cargoes of 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil were steady at around Dec IPE +$9/10 and low sulphur was around Dec +$16/18.
